roles.guarded-by-isinstance: The coercion is preceded by an isinstance(..., int | float) guard that returns/skips before the call, so the argument can never be a string. A comma-formatted string never reaches the float()/int(), so it cannot raise. Safe by construction; not a crash site.

entries.tracked_in: selection.py: _resolve_enrollment_bounds skips any filter whose value is not isinstance(filter_spec.value, int | float) (the `if not isinstance(...): return None` immediately above), so int(filter_spec.value) only ever receives an int/float — never a comma-formatted string. Justified baseline per #1772.
